<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light">
  <title>Black circle</title>
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      background: #fff;
    }
    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 90vmin);
      height: auto;
      overflow: visible;
    }
    @media (forced-colors: active) {
      circle { fill: CanvasText; }
    }
  </style>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 2 2'%3E%3Ccircle cx='1' cy='1' r='1'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <svg width="400" height="400" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
      <title id="circle-title">Black circle</title>
      <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200" fill="#000"/>
    </svg>
  </main>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
I didn't change `0.html` because it's already in good shape and I couldn't find a real problem to fix. It's a single black circle, centred on the page, and it already:

- **Works on phones and small windows:** the circle shrinks to fit the screen (up to 400px wide), and it fills the full screen height on mobile browsers too.
- **Works with screen readers:** the circle is labelled "Black circle", so it's announced properly.
- **Works in high-contrast mode:** the circle switches to the user's text colour.
- **Has a matching tab icon** built into the file, so no extra image is needed.

The only tweaks left would make no visible difference, and I didn't want to churn the file for nothing. If you had a direction in mind, these are the kinds of changes I could make:

1. **Visual:** a different size, colour, gradient or shadow, or an animation such as a pulse or a spin.
2. **Dark mode:** a white circle on a black background when the user's system is set to dark.
3. **Interactivity:** something happens when you hover over or click the circle.
4. **Sharing previews:** a page description and preview image, so the link looks good when posted on social media.

Which of these did you want, or was it something else?
